text:
Ava: Heads-up — customer (Atlassia pilot) asked for a compute-backed throughput add-on: guaranteed 2x burst capacity for 3 1-hour windows / day. Can we map this to product+contract?
Sam: Are they asking for reserved capacity or just priority routing during those windows?
Priya: They specifically said 'guaranteed', so legal will want an SLA. Also asked for price cap if we can't meet it.
Jordan: Technical reality: we can reserve GPU capacity for windows but need a minimum commit. Autoscale can't guarantee instant 2x without cold-start risk unless it's reserved. Tail latency may spike on churn.
Lia: Unit economics: 2x reserved for 3x1h windows daily is a lot. Suggest a minimum monthly commit or a surcharge that covers idle reservation.
Ava: Proposed product compromise: add-on = "burst-reserve" with two modes: "soft-burst" (priority routing + best-effort autoscale) and "hard-reserve" (dedicated reserved pool for windows). Soft priced low, hard priced higher + commit. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Sam: Customers will push for soft at hard prices. We need rollout language to prevent that. Maybe tier gates: only eligible for soft if commit < X, hard if commit >= Y.
Priya: From contract side: require explicit window schedule + 72h change notice; include a remedy that gives credits if we miss windows. Minimal clause sketch below.
Priya: ```
Burst Reserve Add-on: Provider will provision dedicated capacity for Customer's contracted daily windows. Customer must specify windows 30 days in advance. Provider credit = min(20% of daily add-on fee, actual impacted window fees) if guaranteed throughput not met.
```
Jordan: Implementation checklist: 1) scheduling API; 2) placement reservation + isolation; 3) canary rollout to 2 customers; 4) override fallback path to soft-burst.
Lia: Pricing proposal: soft-burst = +15% on top of baseline usage rates; hard-reserve = monthly base fee + usage at 1.1x baseline. Require 3-month minimum for hard-reserve.
Ava: Launch criteria (proposal):
- 2 pilot customers signed for hard-reserve OR 5 for soft-burst
- Perf tests: p99 latency within SLA for 95% of requests during windows
- Billing & schedule UI in Console + schedule API
- Contract language reviewed by legal
If all green, GA flag.
Jordan: Tech Q: do we allow manual override to drop hard-reserve to soft in outages? We need auto-fallback to keep customer traffic flowing. Should be allowed but triggers credits.
Priya: Agreed. Add clause: provider can fail to soft-burst if catastrophic capacity loss, credit applies and customer can terminate add-on after 2 misses.
Sam: I'll push back on price sensitivity with Atlassia — they want a trial month. Could we offer a trial but with reduced guarantees?
Ava: Offer trial with soft-burst only, no guaranteed credit, and require a PO for hard-reserve pilot.

Lia: I'll run unit-econ sims on the Q-2026-1123 numbers and post a short deck tomorrow.
